items.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020
items.q: I was just there — you know turned 21, Art Blakey and the Messengers at the Keystone Korner in San Francisco with Bobby Watson.

ctx.x: Can you describe specifically what a night, taking a bus to hear some music was like for you? Were they nightclubs?

So I’m too young to go to nightclubs, okay? It’s, I think the most perverse thing about my life and career is that I wasn’t 21 until 1971, which means I couldn’t possibly have heard all this great stuff live. I was just there — you know turned 21, Art Blakey and the Messengers at the Keystone Korner in San Francisco with Bobby Watson. You know that’s where I kind of jump into hearing it live. And so what we’re talking about is a fantastic, unbelievable upbringing in rock music in San Francisco. From the age of 14…

Coming to The Fillmore.” And so he took me around to this firehouse where this band was rehearsing with Sears Danelectro amplifiers. And it was Big Brother and the Holding Company before Janis Joplin joined them. And so we would go up there and just listen to them doing these two-chord jams you know, two guitar jams, sorry, not two-chord jams.
